questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x=-A$ and $x=+A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x=0$ to $\frac{A}{2}$ is $2 s$; then time taken by particle in going from $x=\frac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
questions.solution: Let time from 0 to $\mathrm{A} / 2$ is $\mathrm{t}_1$ and from $\mathrm{A} / 2$ to A is $\mathrm{t}_2$ From the standard equation of SHM, $\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}=\mathrm{A} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}_1\right)\Rightarrow \omega t_1=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$ ....(i) Using $x=A_0 \sin \omega t$ again $A=A \sin \omega\left(t_1+t_2\right)\omega\left(t_1+t_2\right)=\sin ^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ Using (i) $\omega t_2=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}$ .....(ii) Dividing equation (i) by (ii) we get $\frac{t_1}{t_2}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \quad t_2=2 t_1=2 \times 2=4 \mathrm{sec}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place R height above earth surface has time period of $T_1=4 \mathrm{~s}$. $T_2$ would be it's time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height $2 R$ from earth surface. Choose the correct relation $[\mathrm{R}=$ radius of Earth $]:$
questions.solution:
Time period of simple pendulum,
$\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{\mathrm{~g}}} \& \mathrm{~g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h})^2}\therefore \mathrm{T} \propto(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h})\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}_1\right)}{\left(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}_2\right)}=\frac{(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{R})}{(\mathrm{R}+2 \mathrm{R})}=\frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{~T}_1=2 \mathrm{~T}_2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The variation of kinetic energy (KE) of a particle executing simple harmonic motion with the displacement (x) starting from mean position to extreme position (A) is given by
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & T \cdot E=K \cdot E+P . E \\ & \Rightarrow K \cdot E=T \cdot E-K \cdot E \\ & =\frac{1}{2} k^2-\frac{1}{2} k^2 \\ & \Rightarrow K E=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2\left(A^2-x^2\right) \quad\left[\because k=m \omega^2\right]\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{KE}$ is maximum at $\mathrm{x}=0$ \& $\mathrm{KE}$ is zero when $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{A}\therefore \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}$ vs $\mathrm{x}$ graph is parabola.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executes SHM of amplitude A. The distance from the mean position when it's kinetic energy becomes equal to its potential energy is
questions.solution:
Let the distance from the mean position is $\mathrm{X}$.
Given $\mathrm{KE}=\mathrm{PE}$
So, $\frac{1}{2} M \omega^2\left(A^2-x^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} M \omega^2 x^2$
$A^2-x^2=x^2 \Rightarrow A^2=2 \times 2$
$\therefore \mathrm{x}= \pm \frac{\mathrm{A}}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a resonance column first and second resonance are obtained at depths $24 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $78 \mathrm{~cm}$ the third resonance will be obtained at depth.
questions.solution:
Given, first resonance column at depth, $l_1=24 \mathrm{~cm}$
Second resonance column at depth, $l_2=78 \mathrm{~cm}$
Third resonance column at depths, $l_3=$ ?
As

\begin{aligned}
& l_1+x=\frac{\lambda}{4}=24 \quad \quad \ldots (i)\\
& l_2+x=\frac{3 \lambda}{4}=78 \quad \quad \ldots (ii)\\
& l_3+x=\frac{5 \lambda}{4}  \quad \quad \ldots (iii)
\end{aligned}

From Eqs. (i) and (ii),

x=\frac{l_2-3 l_1}{2}=\frac{78-3(24)}{2}=3 \quad \quad \ldots (iv)

From Eqs. (iii) and (i), $\frac{l_3+x}{l_1+x}=5$
l_3=5 l_1+5 x-x=5 l_1+4 x

Substituting $l_1$ and $x$ value, we get

l_3=5(24)+4(3) \Rightarrow l_3=132 \mathrm{~cm} .

questions.q: Four massless springs whose force constants are $2 k, 2 k, k$ and $2 k$ respectively are attached to a mass $\mathrm{M}$ kept on a frictionless plane (as shown in figure). If the mass $M$ is displaced in the horizontal direction, then the frequency of the system is?
questions.solution:
The equivalent system is shown in figure.
The equivalent force constant of which $k_{\mathrm{e}}=k+3 k=4 k\therefore \omega=\sqrt{\frac{k_{e}}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 k}{m}}=2 \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$ and $\mathrm{f}=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi}=\frac{2}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$

If $l$ is length of pendulum and $\theta$ be angular amplitude then from principle of conservation of energy

(Initial total energy) $0+\mathrm{mgh}=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}+0$ (Final total energy) $\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2 g h}=\sqrt{2 g l(1-\cos \theta)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The bob of simple pendulum is a spherical hollow ball filled with water. A plugged hole near the bottom of the oscillating bob get suddenly unplugged. During observation, till water is coming out, the time period of oscillation would
options: first increase and then decrease to the original value
first decrease and then increase to the original value
questions.solution:
The bob filled completely with water has its centre of mass at its centre. The time period of oscillation is

T=2πlg

As the water starts coming out of the bob, its centre of mass shifts vertically downward and as a result, effective length of the pendulum increases and hence its period also increases. When the bob is empty, again its centre of mass appears at its centre and as a result, the period of oscillation again reaches to its original value.

=X0-X1=mgk1+2hkmg ,   ∵X1=mgk

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ describe S.H.M. of same amplitude a, same frequency $\mathrm{f}$ along the same straight line. The maximum distance between the two particles is $\mathrm{a} \sqrt{2}$. The initial phase difference between the particle is $-$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{x}_{1}=\mathrm{a} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\phi_{1}\right), \mathrm{x}_{2}=\mathrm{a} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\phi_{2}\right)\Rightarrow \quad\left|\mathrm{x}_{1}-\mathrm{x}_{2}\right|=2 \mathrm{a} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\phi_{1}+\phi_{2}}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\phi_{1}-\phi_{2}}{2}\right)$

Tomaximize $\left|\mathrm{x}_{1}-\mathrm{x}_{2}\right|: \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\phi_{1}+\phi_{2}}{2}\right)=1\Rightarrow \mathrm{a} \sqrt{2}=2 \mathrm{a} \times 1 \times \cos \left(\frac{\phi_{1}-\phi_{2}}{2}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\cos \left(\frac{\phi_{1}-\phi_{2}}{2}\right) \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\phi_{1}-\phi_{2}}{2}\Rightarrow \phi_{1}-\phi_{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}$
